title: Sample a 2-D toy model with the probability-flow ODE
goal:
Implement `pf_ode_sample(score_fn, x_T, n_steps, eps)`, which integrates the probability-flow ODE (Section 4.3, Equation 13) backward in time with Euler steps:

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\tfrac12\beta(t)\,x - \tfrac12\beta(t)\,s(x, t).$$

The times are `ts = np.linspace(1.0, eps, n_steps + 1)`. At step $k$ you are at `t = ts[k]` with step `dt = ts[k + 1] - ts[k]`, which is negative, and you update $x \leftarrow x + \text{drift}(x, t)\,\mathrm{d}t$. The function takes no random generator, because the ODE is deterministic: the same `x_T` always gives the same output.

`score_fn(x, t)` takes `x` of shape `(n, 2)` and a float `t`, and returns the score $\nabla_x \log p_t(x)$. The starter gives you `toy_score`, the exact score of a three-mode Gaussian mixture under the VP-SDE, so no network is needed. The paper uses $\epsilon = 10^{-3}$ for VP SDEs with ODE solvers (Appendix D.4).
hints: Start from `x = x_T.copy()` so the caller's array is not changed.
The Euler update uses the time at the start of the step: `x = x + drift(x, ts[k]) * (ts[k + 1] - ts[k])`.
`dt` is negative. If you write `np.linspace(eps, 1.0, ...)` you integrate in the wrong direction.
The ODE has no noise term. If your function needs a random generator, something is wrong.
